summary: Lisboa is a dense, interlocking Vital Lacerda euro about rebuilding earthquake-ravaged Lisbon, where multi-use cards let you take one of several actions and every building you place has ripple effects across your personal board and the shared city map. It rewards careful long-term planning and engine-building far more than reactive play, and it has a reputation as one of the heaviest, most demanding games in the genre.
praised: strong sense of building a coherent long-term plan
criticised: brutal learning curve and rules overhead
can feel punishing if you fall behind early
not accessible to casual or new gamers

interaction.kind: drafting and market competition, mostly parallel building
interaction.detail: Each player develops their own city area on an individual board, so most construction is private, but goods arrive on a shared central board and are drafted from a common market/warehouse, so taking a good, ship delivery, or card can deny it to others. There is no direct action targeting another player's board.

scoring.how_you_win: Players use multi-use cards to place tiles, produce and sell goods, manage bonds, and fulfill endgame objectives; the game ends when a stack of triggers is exhausted, and the highest total score from all subsystems wins.
